summary: The study focuses on the growth and characterization of ZnO-based buffer layers, specifically Zn1-xMgxO and Zn(O,S), using atomic layer deposition (ALD) for Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) solar cells. The ALD process uses metal-organic precursors and is performed at temperatures below 200 °C. The purpose is to optimize the band alignment between CIGS and the buffer layers to enhance solar cell efficiency by controlling the magnesium and sulfur content in the films.
evidence: The ZnO-based compounds are grown by atomic layer deposition at deposition temperatures below 200 °C using metal-organic precursors. The study focuses on comparing the film growth characteristics of Zn1-xMgxO and Zn(O,S) by ALD. The deposition processes are first characterized and compared to each other for film growth on glass substrates.
